data.title: Instance Metadata Service Reachable from Application
data.summary: The instance metadata endpoint was reachable from application code in its unauthenticated form, so any request-forgery flaw could retrieve the instance role's credentials and act in the cloud account with its privileges.
data.description:
Every cloud instance can query a link-local address for its own metadata, including temporary credentials for the attached role. In the original request-response form, a single unauthenticated HTTP GET returns those credentials.

That makes the metadata service the standard escalation target for SSRF: a flaw that merely fetches a URL becomes cloud account access. The credentials are valid immediately and from anywhere, and their use is difficult to distinguish from the application's own activity.

Session-oriented versions of the service (IMDSv2 and equivalents) require a PUT to obtain a token first and restrict the hop limit, which defeats most request-forgery paths.
data.recommendation:
* Require the session-oriented metadata service and disable the legacy form entirely.
* Set the metadata hop limit to 1 so containers cannot reach it through the host.
* Block outbound access to `169.254.169.254` from application workloads that do not need it.
* Attach minimal roles to instances, so the credentials available are worth little.
* Alert on role credentials used from outside the expected network.
data.short_recommendation: Require IMDSv2 and block link-local access from workloads.
